set.st: On 24 July 1933 a posse surprised the Barrow gang camped on the wooded hill above Dexfield Park. Buck Barrow was mortally wounded and Blanche Barrow captured; Clyde Barrow, Bonnie Parker and W. D. Jones escaped. Forum tellings say up to $65,000 in loot was buried near the camp. No period record of any cache has been found, and the gang's known takings were far smaller. Pin circle (500 m) is on 'The Dexfield Park Co.' tract of the 1916 county atlas, on the sec. 17/18 line; not the spot itself.
set.t: The shootout is well documented; the loot is not. Period papers for 25-31 July 1933 (Dexter, Adel, Des Moines) are being read for what money was found on the gang. On the 1930 aerial the Raccoon River runs about 1.5 km north of the 1916 tract label, through sec. 8, with wooded bluffs between; the camp hill and the park grounds may lie anywhere in that band. No digging; look-only.
pinev: Dexfield Park Co. tract, 1916 Dallas Co atlas Union Twp; on the sec. 17/18 line T78N R29W (BLM PLSS). The atlas places it on the south side of the Raccoon, but the 1930 aerial puts the river about 1.5 km north in sec. 8, so conf C until the park grounds are matched on the aerial.

set.n: Convict's robbery gold on Five Mile Hill, Grand Haven (1874 tale; 1899-1900 digs)
set.pl: Five Mile Hill: crest of the big dune south of the Grand Haven harbour, behind the old lighthouse ground
set.st: About 1874 a Jackson prison convict told Ottawa County coroner Curtis W. Gray he had buried several thousand dollars of robbery gold 'in the hill immediately back of the light house', beside a described tree on Light House Hill. Gray and Marshal Ike Sanford dug and found nothing. In October 1899 N. Stebbins and Col. William C. Baty of Pueblo, Colorado, searched the hill with 'metal instruments'; five days later the Tribune wrote that 'many persons in town believe that Col. Baty the treasure hunter found the gold he was searching after.' In April 1900 Baty returned with a Mr. Robinson and two labourers and sank a planked shaft from the crest of Five Mile Hill, the big dune south of the harbour; after three weeks, a 90-ft hole and 3,000 ft of lumber in the curbing, he quit on 7 May 1900 with nothing, and the hole was to be filled. Pin is the crest of the hill, not a cache spot.
set.t: The 1899 'Baty found it' rumour is answered by his 1900 return: three digs (1874, 1899, 1900) found nothing. The 1874 confession is second-hand. City park and Coast Guard ground: look-only.
pinev: Five Mile Hill crest, named in the 1900 Tribune; Baty's 90-ft shaft was sunk from the crest. Crest is the highest point of the dune mass south of the harbour on 2016 Michigan 1 m lidar (237.7 m).
